question: Design a Redis-backed login session including TTL and what happens on Redis restart.
questionBn: TTLসহ Redis-backed লগইন সেশন ডিজাইন করুন এবং Redis রিস্টার্টে কী হয় বলুন।
shortAnswer: Store session id → user payload with EX/TTL; rotate ids on login; treat Redis as ephemeral—users re-auth if data is lost unless persistence is configured and accepted.
strongAnswer: Generate a high-entropy session id, SET with EX (absolute or sliding refresh). Avoid storing passwords. For sliding expiry, refresh TTL on activity carefully. Document durability: without AOF/RDB expectations, restarts drop sessions. Sensitive apps may store server-side session metadata in Postgres and use Redis as a cache.
followUps: How do you implement a safe distributed lock with SET NX EX?
commonWrongAnswer: Store sessions forever without TTL to improve UX.
productionRelevance: Session and rate-limit patterns are ubiquitous in Nest/Express APIs.
integrationProcedure: 1) Reproduce the scenario in a small spike using Redis, Sessions. 2) Write the strong answer as an ADR or PR description. 3) Add a test or monitor that would catch the common wrong answer in production. 4) Document rollback/owner. 5) Rehearse the follow-ups aloud once.
